text:
marco: Hey, noticed intermittent 503s for api.redwood.ai in eu-west-1 after the cert rotation. TLS handshake succeeds but client sees the wrong cert (CN=redwood.ai). Happening across a bunch of pods behind the ALB. Any ideas?

anya: grabbing logs, seeing ALB return certificate for root domain while Host header is api.redwood.ai. browser shows CN mismatch.

kevin: did we switch to a wildcard cert or a new ACM cert earlier? deploy-bot just pushed a cert refresh at 12:03 UTC.

deploy-bot: cert-rotation job completed 2026-03-18T12:03:05Z, ACM arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/abcd-ef01, target listeners: 443.

marco: ACM ARN matches the new cert. But behavior sounds like ALB SNI selection hitting a fallback cert. ALB should pick cert by SNI. Maybe we exceeded SAN/wildcard limits?

zhen: quick check: `aws elbv2 describe-listeners --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:listener/xxx` shows certificates: [arn:..., arn:...]. ALB supports multiple certs but there is an internal limit and ordering can matter for overlapping SANs.

kevin: also confirm that api.redwood.ai CNAME -> alb DNS and Route53 health checks are green. If ALB healthcheck is failing, target group might be returning 503s (not cert mismatch). Are we seeing TLS-level mismatch or HTTP 503 from target group?

anya: curl -v https://api.redwood.ai --resolve "api.redwood.ai:443:54.12.34.56" shows certificate CN=root redwood.ai, then GET fails with 503 from target group. So two problems: SNI returned wrong cert and the backend returned 503 (health check flapping).

marco: possible chain: ALB picks wrong cert (client handshake uses wrong cert) because SNI routing used default cert when SNI not matched. Some clients (old clients or mTLS test harness) might not send SNI or ALB sees conflicting SANs and picks default. Also we recently enabled mTLS on some routes which required TCP passthrough -> that configuration could have forced a different listener.

sre-oncall: important: ACM certs are regional. We have a cross-region DNS entry pointing to CloudFront in front of ALB for some domains, but api.redwood.ai is regional ALB. Double-check envs: eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1 mismatch can cause CloudFront to cache old cert or route to a different ALB.

zhen: config snippet from k8s ingress that could be relevant:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/certificate-arn: arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:...
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTPS":443}]'
    alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/ssl-redirect: '443'
spec:
  rules:
  - host: api.redwood.ai
    http:
      paths: ...
```
If the ingress controller had stale annotation it might not have updated the ALB listener order.

kevin: actionable checks I'm going to run: 1) `aws elbv2 describe-ssl-policies` and `describe-listeners` to confirm certificate ARNs + order, 2) `aws acm describe-certificate` to inspect SANs, 3) verify Route53 alias points to correct ALB DNS.

anya: I also see some mTLS tests failing where curl with `--cert client.pem` works only when we use TLS passthrough (NLB->pod) not ALB TLS-terminate. Our recent attempt to centralize TLS at ALB may have broken mTLS flows because ALB cannot do mTLS to backend unless we terminate and re-initiate client cert validation at app layer.

marco: TL;DR likely causes: SNI fallback due to overlapping SANs/wildcard + stale ingress annotations + region/cdn routing mismatch + mTLS termination expectations.

kevin: quick mitigation: 1) add explicit ALB listener certificate precedence by removing ambiguous certs (take out wildcard with overlapping SANs), 2) if mTLS is required for certain paths, route them via a dedicated NLB listener with TCP passthrough, 3) rotate DNS TTLs lower while we fix routing. I'll start removing the extra cert from the listener and flip healthchecks to HTTP/200 path for a bit.

zhen: note: ALB has a hard limit on 25 certs per listener and when cert names overlap SNI selection can be non-deterministic. For many subdomains prefer one multi-SAN cert or separate listeners per domain if you need deterministic selection.

sre-oncall: I'll monitor errors and flip on a canary after kevin's change. If we need immediate rollback, revert the cert-rotation by reattaching previous cert ARN.

marco: assigning owners: kevin -> ALB cert/listener changes, zhen -> ingress annotations + k8s controller sync, anya -> healthcheck/backends and mTLS test runs, sre-oncall -> monitoring + rollback. We'll reconvene in 30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

(30m later)
anya: Update: removed overlapping wildcard cert from listener. ALB is now serving api.redwood.ai cert for SNI requests. Backend 503s dropped after fixing a health check path mismatch (`/healthz` was 302 -> changed to 200). mTLS test still failing for TCP terminated paths — moving that traffic to dedicated NLB as planned.

marco: Great, sounds like resolved enough to re-open canary. Thanks all. We'll document the pattern: no overlapping wildcard+multi-SANs on same ALB listener, prefer NLB passthrough for mTLS, and ensure ingress controller annotations are authoritative.
